_note: Watershed rebuild parameters (docs/water/watershed_rebuild_design.md). One file for every stage, so a run is reproduced from it and the input hashes in its manifest.

uplift._note: Stage A2: where and how fast the land rose (m/yr). Design part: high where the landform is high, from the smoothed landform. Structural part: plane-wave variation at kilometre scale only (2.4 and 1.1 km), the scale at which uplift really varies. Hills and valleys below a kilometre are NOT put in here: they come from the erosion itself, which spaces valleys by the balance of stream cutting and soil creep (document sections 10 and 11: terrain shaped by water, variety from conditions, not random). Sonny 7 Nov 19:30, holistic review: the 520 m and 230 m octaves were removed because uplift bumps at hill scale would make hills that the water did not shape.

rain._note: Stage A4: Smith and Barstad (2004) linear orographic rain on a coarse grid, then smoothed up to the model grid. Wind direction per tile row comes from the landform manifest (climate.wind_toward_x). background_mm_yr is the rain far from relief (not yet measured for our climate; a temperate maritime value).

rock._note: Stage A3: rock ids from the geology export (export_geology.gd --step equal to the model cell). Soluble rocks may hold karst (cave springs, stage C7).

evolve._note: Stage B (evolve.py). K, m and D follow the earlier pre-carve runs (tools/erosion_precarve real_run: K 4e-6, m 0.5, D 0.05 m2/yr). G is the dimensionless deposition coefficient (about 1: deposition matters, floodplains and fans form). channel_area_m2: no fluvial cutting below this drainage area (2 ha), so the smallest hollows are shaped by creep, not gullied. Not yet tuned on our island: R2's first run sets them.
